title: My roommate hasn't left her room in six days. She still answers me every time I knock.
story:
Dani's door has been shut since last Wednesday. I keep a list on the fridge, because it helps me stay calm. Day one, she said she had the flu. Day two, she asked me to leave soup outside the door.

By day four the soup was still there, untouched, but she kept answering when I knocked. Her voice came through the wood, cheerful. "I'm fine. Just tired."

On day five I noticed something. She used the exact same words every time. Just tired. I'm fine. Just tired.

Then I noticed worse. The sentences were mine. The way I say fine, with the little sigh at the end.

Last night I knocked and said, "Dani, are you okay?"

And through the door, in my voice, came, "Dani, are you okay?"

I stood there, not breathing. Then, in a whisper, she answered from the far corner of the room. Her real voice. Thin, scared, close to the floor.

"Please don't open it. It only learns from what you say."

Under the door, the light flickered, as something stood up.

In my voice, it said, "Open it."

I haven't said a word since.
premise: roommate answers from the room but the voice is made of my own phrases
